methods.label: Subtract to remove the common remainder
methods.explanation:
When two integers have the same remainder upon division by \(N\), subtracting them cancels that remainder. Their difference must therefore be a multiple of \(N\).

Thus \(N\) divides both
\[90-69=21\qquad\text{and}\qquad125-90=35.\]
The positive common divisors of \(21\) and \(35\) are \(1\) and \(7\). Since \(N>1\), we must have \(N=7\). This works: \(69\), \(90\), and \(125\) each leave remainder \(6\) when divided by \(7\).

Finally,
\[81=11\cdot7+4,\]
so \(81\) is congruent to \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
